title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative: The Government of Saudi Arabia (KSA) is currently undertaking substantial transformation, aimed at diversifying the economy to reduce reliance on oil exports, promote private sector growth, and stimulate job creation, amidst efforts to nationalize the workforce, increase women's participation in the labour market, including modernize infrastructure and attract foreign investment. However, the absence of a legal framework aligned to the Fundamental Principals and Rights at Work (FPRW), mainly workers' right to establish trade unions and the limited social dialogue are among the areas that require attention in order to meet its objectives and achieve decent work. Since 2001, through the ILO support the Government of KSA allowed Saudi workers in big enterprises to establish "workers committees", as a substitute for trade unions; however, migrant workers, who represent the majority of workers in the private sector, were excluded. In November 2010, the Government enabled the establishment of the National Worker’s Committee (NWC) as a transition body towards the formation of a “National Federation for Trade Unions”. Later in 2019, pushed by the fact that the Kingdom is chairing the G20 summit. The Government issued a decision nominating a new leadership for the National Workers’ Committee and approached the ILO to engage the NWC in the planned activities of the signed project that aims at developing the capacities of the Ministry of Human Resource and Social Development. The ILO used this opportunity to promote FPRW and develop the enabling environment for constructive and inclusive social dialogue based on ILS, including the creation of tripartite institutions in the Kingdom. The ILO under this outcome will support the NWC efforts to develop its capacities, and structures to expand its representativeness among new groups of workers through improved and innovative services to transform into a full-fledged trade union organization.
